analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 598-1011), so the PR changes documentation only. No executable code, authorization logic, crypto or schema is visible, and no concrete security regression can be cited from this text. The changelog describes behaviour implemented in other files that this pass did not see.

Claims the next pass should check against code (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, T-052..T-058):
- Lines 633-635: App Attest dead-key rotation after two consecutive DeviceCheck code-0/2 failures. Limits are one rotation per machine per hour and four per 24 hours. Rotation admission is serialized with machine merges, and the 6-hour invalidKey backoff is a separate control. Rotated keys must still pass attestation, receipt, build qualification and assertion. The text says rotation never revokes or denies serving. Verify that a provider cannot induce rotation, so that it escapes a revocation or tombstone tied to the old key (T-053/T-055), and that the budget really carries across machine merges.
- Lines 638, 642-647: untrusted ready-reply diagnostics (launch_session, boot_time, operation_stalled_seconds, error chains, push history). They are said to sit outside the signed transcript and to have no authorization effect. The provider-triggered self-restart is gated by idle state and a 6-hour limit. Verify that coordinator parsing drops invalid values and that the diagnostics cannot influence authorization.
- Line 644: `darkbloom report` under sudo reads the invoking user's credentials and state file. Verify that the upload scope and redaction do not leak tokens (T-058).
- Line 645: code_attest metrics carry no provider, device or token identifiers in their tags.
- Line 637: durable Apple device-attestation chain staged for macOS 27 candidates. It attaches only after hardware trust, re-verifies to Apple's root and binds this connection's SE key (TB-009/T-036).
- Line 668: signed 20-byte CandidateCDHash unique-match to the approved full 32-byte CodeDirectory hash (T-054).
- Lines 740, 749, 754: macOS 27+ skips MDM enrollment, and removal requires fresh coordinator approval (T-057).
- Lines 665 and 687: the attestation roster excludes private-only providers, and the live authorization snapshot is consistent (T-058).

The changelog does not require a threat-model update on its own.
